NOAA prohibits sexual assault and sexual harassment by or of any employee, supervisor, manager, contractor, vendor, affiliate, or other individual with whom NOAA employees come into contact by the virtue of their work for NOAA. (a) Definitions. Contractor Employees - The term “contractor employees,” as used in this solicitation and contract language, refers to employees of the prime contractor or its subcontractors, affiliates, consultants, or team members. Sexual Assault - The term sexual assault, as used in this solicitation and contract language, means any conduct proscribed by state or federal sexual abuse laws, including, but not limited to, those defined in chapter 109A of title 18 of the U.S. Code (sexual abuse), and assaults committed both by offenders who are strangers to the victim and by offenders who are known or related by blood or marriage to the victim. Sexual Harassment - As defined by the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission, sexual harassment is a form of sex discrimination that violates Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964. The Northwest Fisheries Science Center (NWFSC) Environmental Chemistry Program (ECP) requires a comprehensive multi-year service and support agreement for its AB SCIEX ExionLC AE liquid chromatographer coupled with QTRAP 5500 tandem mass spectrometer (LC-MS/MS) systems. The requirement comprises one base year and 3 subsequent option years to ensure uninterrupted operational capacity. The service contract must include, at minimum: 1. Preventative Maintenance (PM): The PM has to be conducted by AB Sciex certified field engineers to ensure the system operates within Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) specifications. One annual on-site visit for both LC and MS systems. Replacements of parts with OEM parts. 2. Corrective Repair: Unlimited on-site repairs conducted by AB Sciex certified field engineers to assure instrument returns to its peak performance and OEM specifications. On-site repair within 2 business days from the call for LC systems and 3 business days for MS systems. All service repairs will be performed by AB SCIEX’s certified field engineer. 3. deliverables_scope.text:
1. Introduction

The African Union Development Agency – New Partnership for Africa Development (AUDA-NEPAD) has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the “Resilient Irrigation for a Sustainable Economy Project”, and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services. “Consultancy Services to Develop and Deploy the Africa RISE Gateway”

 

  1. Description of Services

The consulting services (“the Services”) include: Task 1: Africa RISE User Requirements Assessment: Map and profile all user groups and partners including relevant African Union agencies and departments (AUDANEPAD, AU-SAFGRAD, SEBE), government ministries, transboundary water management agencies, regulators, MPA focal points, implementing partners, research institutes and universities and technical experts, farmers, aggregators, private sector, equipment suppliers and financial institutions and farmer unions and cooperative societies etc; Task 2: Design, Develop and Commission the Africa RISE Gateway: Define system architecture, data structures, modules, dashboard requirements and proc

ISE User Requirements Assessment: Map and profile all user groups and partners including relevant African Union agencies and departments (AUDANEPAD, AU-SAFGRAD, SEBE), government ministries, transboundary water management agencies, regulators, MPA focal points, implementing partners, research institutes and universities and technical experts, farmers, aggregators, private sector, equipment suppliers and financial institutions and farmer unions and cooperative societies etc; Task 2: Design, Develop and Commission the Africa RISE Gateway: Define system architecture, data structures, modules, dashboard requirements and process workflows, including a unified data interoperability Layer that meets vPIC standards and aligns with the Africa RISE Regional Geospatial Analytics Platform and national irrigation monitoring systems.  The architecture shall specify: (a) the endpoints and payload schemas through which national data collection tools, the Regional Geospatial Platform,  and other authorized external data sources submit and validate benchmarking data; (b) the data lineage and version control mechanisms ensuring that published benchmarks are traceable to their submission source; and (c) the traffic-light alert logic that translates performanc

sociated training materials for all user groups, comprising: (i) a Technical Track for AUDA-NEPAD IT personnel, national technical focal points and system administrators, covering system administration, data management, integration and cybersecurity; (ii) an Operational Track for programme managers, extension officers and policy stakeholders, focusing on effective use of the platform and its functional modules; and (iii) an End-User Track providing simplified guidance and orientation materials. Task 4: Sustainable Operation and Maintenance (O&M) Model for the Gateway: Assess the technical and operational requirements for sustained operation of the Gateway, including hosting, security, data management, updates, user support and maintenance schedules and prepare indicative annual cost projections for the post-project period. Task 5: Envisaged functionality of the Africa RISE Gateway: The Africa RISE Gateway, as a go-to information and knowledge solution, is envisaged to serve.

 

  1. Level of Effort for Key staff:

STATEMENT OF WORK C. 1. OVERVIEW/BACKGROUND. The Library of Congress (Library) requires a contractor to produce, maintain, and support the latest generation of Digital Talking Book Machine (DTBM) devices, known as the DA2 (DTBM model Digital Advanced version 2), which were originally launched June 18, 2025. The National Library Service for the Blind and Print Disabled (NLS) provides free books and magazines in audio and braille format to eligible U.S. residents and citizens living abroad. NLS’ enabling legislation was changed in 2016 (Public Law 114-219) to permit NLS to develop and distribute devices to be used for reading any format, including DAISY (Digital Accessible Information System). As part of these services and products offered, NLS loans free DTBMs for use in consuming NLS-produced audio materials. NLS-produced audio materials are distributed via NLS DTBM cartridges and data files online via Braille and Audio Reading Download (BARD) website in AMR-WB+, MPEG I/Layer 3 (MP3), RIFF WAV, and other audio formats. NLS requires additional DA2 units, consistent with the existing inventory

The Library of Congress (Library) requires a contractor to produce, maintain, and support the latest generation of Digital Talking Book Machine (DTBM) devices, known as the DA2 (DTBM model Digital Advanced version 2), which were originally launched June 18, 2025. The National Library Service for the Blind and Print Disabled (NLS) provides free books and magazines in audio and braille format to eligible U.S. residents and citizens living abroad. NLS’ enabling legislation was changed in 2016 (Public Law 114-219) to permit NLS to develop and distribute devices to be used for reading any format, including DAISY (Digital Accessible Information System). As part of these services and products offered, NLS loans free DTBMs for use in consuming NLS-produced audio materials. NLS-produced audio materials are distributed via NLS DTBM cartridges and data files online via Braille and Audio Reading Download (BARD) website in AMR-WB+, MPEG I/Layer 3 (MP3), RIFF WAV, and other audio formats. NLS requires additional DA2 units, consistent with the existing inventory of NLS DA2 devices. NLS requires quantities suffi

f_Work.docx ===== STATEMENT OF WORK (SOW) RFID Cabinet The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Veterans Health Administration (VHA), requires the acquisition of a Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) storage cabinet integrated with Unique Device Identifier (UDI)-compliant tissue and implant tracking software to support patient safety, regulatory compliance, and efficient inventory management. Tracking tissues, biologics, and implantable medical devices is a federal regulatory requirement under FDA 21 CFR Part 830 (UDI) and is critical to patient safety. VA healthcare facilities face ongoing resource challenges including staff shortages and budget constraints, making it essential to minimize staff time consumed by manual data entry and to maintain precise control over high-value inventory. This acquisition will provide an automated, real-time RFID-based inventory management solution for use in the operating room (OR), Catheterization (Cath) lab, ambulatory surgery center, or any facility location that stores high-value implantable inventory. Description The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Veterans Health Administration (VHA), requires one (1) InVita UDTracker® RFID Cabinet — consisting of Terso Solutions RFID cabinet hardware integrated with InVita's UDTracker® tissue and implant
